title: small-packet-interleaving-tail-latency-study
content:
Summary:

This doc captures an ad-hoc investigation into recurring p95/p99 tail latency spikes observed in multi-GPU inference pods when small control/KV-cache tensors are interleaved with large attention/key-value tensor transfers. The workload is our 7B/13B streaming chat pipeline with prefix KV cache updates and simultaneous batched generation. Symptoms were short (50-200ms) but high-magnitude tail spikes that increase overall request latency despite stable average throughput.

Why this matters:
- Customer-facing interactive latency is dominated by p95/p99, not mean. These micro-tail events degrade UX and increase cost (retries, longer held resources).
- The behavior appears sensitive to the pattern of small vs large inter-GPU transfers and fabric topology (NVLink/NVSwitch vs PCIe-only).

Experiment context and motivation:
- Trigger: alerts from /observability/route/chat-streaming showing p99 jumps from ~120ms -> 300ms on certain clusters when KV-cache hit rate increases (more small writes).
- Hypothesis: small-packet bursts (KV updates, small gradients, control messages) are being serialized behind bulk transfers on the interconnect; congestion and serialization cause driver/NCCL scheduling delays and kernel stalls.

Hardware / SW baseline:
- Nodes: 8x A100-80GB with NVSwitch (NVLink fabric) and 4x A100-40GB with PCIe-only (two distinct testbeds)
- OS and drivers: Ubuntu 22.04, CUDA 12.1, NVIDIA driver 535.xx
- NCCL: 2.17.3 release build used by runtime containers
- Serving runtime: rwd-infer/runtime v0.28.1 (with default NCCL launch and baseline batching)
- Workload: chat streaming repeated tokens; KV cache updates (~4–8 small tensors of 512–2kB each) interleaved with attention KV transfers (~tens of MBs).

Microbench methodology:
1) Replay request trace with controlled KV frequency: baseline (no KV writes), low (1 small burst every 200ms), high (1 small burst every 50ms).
2) Synthetic bench: interleave small NCCL AllReduce (1–8KB) with large AllGather (20–80MB) with varying concurrency.
3) Collect: per-GPU GPU timeline, NCCL trace (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO), nvprof/nvtx markers from runtime, and tcpdump-like capture of PCIe/NVLink-level events when possible (using nsys).
4) Measure latency percentiles across millions of requests; capture kernel wait times and stream blocking metrics.

Key observations (NVSwitch cluster):
- Baseline: p50=12ms, p95=36ms, p99=92ms.
- High small-burst condition: p50=13ms, p95=58ms, p99=230ms.
- NCCL timeline shows short AllReduce completions for small tensors frequently queued behind long-running AllGather kernels used for KV/activations.
- NVSwitch traces reveal that when a large NVLink transfer is in flight between certain pairs, small transfers involving the same intermediary switches can be delayed by 1–3x full-link RTT (tens of microseconds each) — cumulative effect produces 100+ms tail across multiple sequential steps in the pipeline.
- GPU-side kernel logs show streams blocked waiting on device-to-device memcopy completion events.

Key observations (PCIe-only cluster):
- Baseline: p50=14ms, p95=44ms, p99=120ms.
- High small-burst: p50=15ms, p95=78ms, p99=340ms (worse than NVSwitch).
- PCIe shows larger serialization: small transfers queued behind host DMA bursts from large tensor transfers; OS DMA engine contention and PCIe credit exhaustion scenarios observed in nsys capture.

NCCL behavior and environment notes:
- NCCL uses multiple rings and opportunistic scheduling; small messages often take the same rings as big messages unless ring partitioning is changed.
- Setting NCCL_MIN_NRINGS=4 reduced p99 by ~18% in NVSwitch runs (kept other params same).
- NCCL_P2P_LEVEL and disabling specific transports had mixed results; disabling IB or enabling SOCKET for fallback increased latency unpredictably and is not viable for production.

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
1) Cross-traffic serialization: large allgathers monopolize the fabric/rings and either preempt or delay scheduling of small messages, producing queueing delays across multiple sequence steps.
2) Microburst/credit exhaustion: rapid succession of large packets plus many small packets leads to NVSwitch/PCIe credit starvation events, which introduce retransmission-worthy stalls.
3) Driver-side scheduling granularity: CUDA/NCCL kernel scheduling and host-side submission order cause small-message kernels to be submitted slower when large DMA kernels are in flight.
4) Runtime-level concurrency: our current runtime issues concurrent inter-node collectives without awareness of message size, so it unknowingly increases head-of-line blocking.

Evidence supporting hypotheses:
- Correlation between large-transfer duration on NCCL timeline and delayed small-message completions.
- p99 spikes align with bursts of small writes (KV cache flush pattern) following a large attention transfer.
- Reconfiguring NCCL rings had a measurable effect; suggests rings are a major factor.

Quick mitigations tried (non-invasive):
- Batching small KV updates into a single aggregated tensor at runtime before issuing the collective: improved p99 by ~25% in controlled runs but incurred slight added serialization latency for single small writes.
- Introduced 1ms pacing between large and small collectives (synthetic throttling) — eliminated most extreme tails but reduced throughput slightly (~3%).
- Set NCCL_MIN_NRINGS=4 in runtime container env: reduced p99 by ~18% without observable throughput regression.

Longer-term mitigations to evaluate:
- Priority-aware collective scheduling: create a lightweight control ring for sub-8KB messages that gets higher priority at the runtime/NCCL layer (requires NCCL or driver support or dedicated small-message ring assignment).
- Hardware-aware placement: schedule KV-update-heavy requests on nodes/topologies where small-message latency is known to be low (e.g., avoiding PCIe-only nodes for high-KV workloads).
- Runtime-level message coalescing: always aggregate tiny tensors within a request boundary; add heuristic to keep aggregation delay under 1–2ms to bound added latency.
- Per-GPU egress shaping: enforce rate limits for bulk transfers to reduce credit exhaustion risk (needs testing for throughput impact).
- Kernel launch stream partitioning: ensure small-message kernels get their own non-blocked CUDA streams and use cudaStreamPriority where supported.

Planned experiments (next sprints):
1) Controlled ring assignment sweep: run matrix of NCCL ring counts and NCCL_NVLINK_P2P settings across NVSwitch and PCIe beds; measure p50/p95/p99 and throughput. Owner: Miguel. ETA: 2w.
2) Aggregation threshold tuning: evaluate latency vs aggregation delay tradeoff (thresholds 1KB/4KB/16KB; max hold time 0.5/1/2ms). Owner: Priya. ETA: 1.5w.
3) Pacing policy test: implement soft pacing in runtime that adds nanosecond-scale gaps between large-chunk DMA submissions and measure tail impact. Owner: Sana. ETA: 2w.
4) Driver/NCCL upgrade test: validate on NCCL 2.18+ nightly and CUDA 12.2 driver combos; collate any fixes or regressions. Owner: Ethan. ETA: 3w.

Repro steps for engineers:
1) Checkout rwd-infer/runtime branch small-packet-experiments.
2) Run scripts/bench/interleave_bench.sh with args: --mode synthetic --small-size 2048 --large-size 40000000 --small-frequency 20 --duration 600
3) Capture traces: export NCCL_DEBUG=TRACE, nvtx markers enabled, run nsys for 60s during steady state.
4) Check reports in artifacts/bench-output for p50/p95/p99 and for NCCL ring utilization logs.

Action items and owners (short-term):
- Add an option in runtime to automatically aggregate small tensors per request (Priya, PR #1428).
- Add a knob for NCCL_MIN_NRINGS in deployment templates and roll to canary (Miguel).
- Schedule driver/NCCL upgrade tests in staging (Ethan).
- Postmortem writeup and customer-facing note draft if needed (Sana).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Does NVSwitch internal arbitration prioritize certain packet sizes? Hardware docs are unclear; may require vendor engagement.
- Are there firmware updates that change credit behavior for our node types? Need to check with infra/partners.
- Is there a safe way to expose a small-message priority ring in NCCL without upstream changes?

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Try cudaStreamCreateWithPriority for small-message kernels — may give quick wins on GPU scheduling side without touching NCCL.
- Evaluate whether our KV cache protocol can be further relaxed (send deltas less often) for production when customers tolerate micro-latency vs freshness tradeoffs.

Appendix (raw snippet from NCCL trace):
- [TIMESTAMP] rank0 rank1 AllGather start large (size 42MB)
- [TIMESTAMP+12ms] rank2 rank3 small AllReduce start (size 2KB) queued -> start delayed 85ms
- Device timeline: cudaMemcpy peer wait event duration 86ms

References and tickets:
- SERV-2912 (investigate tail spikes on chat-streaming)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1428 (small-tensor-aggregation)

If you want to reproduce a specific offending trace I captured, ping me and I will share nsys exports (large, ~120MB) — they live in /mnt/artifacts/experiments/small-packet-2025-02.
